releases.title: A tidier map
notes: Map labels no longer pile on top of each other: your stays and regions always get their names, and province names only show where there’s room — zoom in to see more.

releases.title: A workspace for big screens
notes: On a laptop or desktop (1200 px and wider), a trip now uses the whole screen: the map on the left with your regions underneath, the timeline in the middle, and “At a glance” on the right — your to-dos, unplanned nights and packing.
Click a step or region and its details open on the right, so you never lose your place in the timeline.
The map follows along as you scroll, and hovering a card highlights its pin. The Map tab still opens the big full-screen map.
Everywhere: a cleaner look — plain paper instead of the squared background, and no more dashed lines under things you can edit (hover to see them, tap to change).

releases.title: Trip to-dos
notes: Every trip now has a To-do list — a new To-do tab next to Packing. Add anything (it doesn’t have to belong to a step), tick it off, tap to rename it, or delete it; finished ones fold away under “N done”.
Ask Claude to manage it too: “add ‘buy travel insurance’ to the Thailand to-dos”, “what’s still open?”, “tick off the passport check”.
Deleted to-dos land in Trash, so you can bring them back.

releases.title: Tabs that stay put
notes: When you scroll the timeline (or a step’s details), the tabs and the back link now sit on their own pinned bar at the top, instead of floating over your cards.

releases.title: See your regions on the map
notes: The map now shows where your regions are: the provinces you’re staying in are shaded, and each region is labelled.
On the Map tab, tap a region (All · Bangkok · North · …) to zoom to it and see it highlighted — tap All to see the whole trip again.
Shading works for Thailand, France, Belgium, the USA and Japan today; elsewhere you still get the region labels.

releases.title: Plan by region
notes: Every region now has its own page — tap the › on a region to rename it, set planned nights or dates, add a note, see all its steps, move it earlier or later, or delete it.
Add a region straight from the timeline (“add region” at the bottom) — handy for sketching “Bangkok 4 nights → North 5 nights” before anything is booked.
Move a step into a region from its details, and new steps can be added into a region directly.
Budget now breaks your costs down by region, and deleted regions show up in Trash so you can bring them back.
The timeline’s Show control is simpler: Regions · Locations · Steps, plus a one-tap Expand all / Collapse all.

releases.title: A real menu, more room
notes: The ☰ button now opens a small menu with Home and What’s New — the sidebar that used to hold them is gone, so the page gets the whole width (and phones lose a row).
On every trip page the Timeline · Map · Budget · Packing tabs now sit right at the top, in the same place on all four.

releases.title: Smoother timeline, fewer dead ends
notes: Tapping a step’s title or its › inside a region opens it again — and the regions and places you opened stay open when you come back.
Tapping a region in the nights strip now lands on that region’s header, not halfway into it.
The Timeline · Map · Budget · Packing tabs stay pinned right under the top bar while you scroll, on phones too — and there’s no longer a white bar behind them.
A region with just one place opens straight to its stay in one tap.
Packing, Budget and Home are back on plain paper — the map only shows behind the itinerary and in the Map tab.

releases.title: Your trip, region by region
notes: The timeline is now grouped the way you think about a trip: regions (like “North” or “Krabi”), the places you stay in each, and the steps inside them. Tap a region or place to open or close it.
Use “Show” at the top to see the whole trip at a glance by regions, by places, or every step.
A summary line and a strip of nights per region sit above the timeline — tap a region in the strip to jump to it.
Nights with nothing planned show up as their own “N nights unplanned” marker, so gaps are easy to spot (an overnight train or flight counts as covered).
Claude can now set up and edit regions for you: ask it to group your stays, rename a region, or move one earlier or later.
A Feedback tab on the right edge of the screen lets you send a quick note about whatever you’re looking at.

releases.title: See your trip on the map
notes: Your itinerary now has a map: a soft world atlas sits behind the timeline with a pin on every stay, so you can see the shape of the trip at a glance.
A new Map tab opens the whole trip full-screen — drag to pan, pinch or scroll to zoom, and tap any pin to jump straight to that stay’s details.
The map appears once a stay has a location: paste a Google Maps link with coordinates when adding a stay (or ask Claude to set them) and its pin shows up.
It’s all self-hosted and private — no map provider, no tracking, no extra cost — and it re-tints for light and dark automatically.

releases.title: See how long — and find your way back
notes: Every timeline card now shows its duration at a glance — nights for a stay, travel time for a leg — so you can scan how long you’re spending where.
Opening an activity and tapping “back” now returns you to the step it belongs to, instead of jumping to the trip home.

releases.title: Remove an activity
notes: You can now delete an activity: tap the trash icon on it in a stay’s list, or use “Delete activity” on its detail page.
Deleted activities go to Trash, so you can restore them if you change your mind.

releases.title: A photo behind your stay
notes: Pin a photo to a stay and it becomes the background of that stay’s card on the timeline — so scrolling your trip shows the view behind each place you’re staying.
Open a stay’s detail, then tap the pin button on any of its photos to set it as the background; pinning another photo replaces it, and tapping again unpins.
Text stays easy to read over any photo — a warm scrim keeps the title, dates and status legible in both light and dark mode.
Travel legs stay clean and text-only; only stays get a background photo.
Claude can do it too: ask it to pin a photo (the new pin_image tool).

releases.title: Deeper budgets & detail pages
notes: Tap any travel leg or stay to open its own detail page — with its activities, photos, notes and everything editable, just like activities already had.
Budget “Where it goes” now flips between Estimated and Actual, so you can see planned spend versus what you’ve really paid.
New Budget Insights: cost per person (split two ways for now).
Mark a cost as “included in another ticket” (on a step or activity) — it’s hidden on the card and left out of the budget, so bundled fares don’t double-count.
Locations now use real Google Maps links: paste a Maps link when adding a step/activity, or let Claude set the exact place — with coordinates as a fallback.

releases.title: Plan it yourself
notes: Build your trip right in the app: tap “add step” anywhere on the timeline to insert a stay or a travel leg through a quick guided wizard — no need to ask Claude.
Add activities the same way: an “add activity” button on each stay opens a short wizard for the title, day, cost, booking status and more.
Setting a location is easy — just paste a Google Maps link (or “lat, lng”) and the wizard pulls out the coordinates.
Map links now open Google Maps instead of OpenStreetMap.
More things are tap-to-edit inline: cost estimates, activity dates, and each step’s dates and times — with native date/time pickers.
Status chips open on a single tap now (no more double-tap to change Idea → Booked).
Travel legs show the date and the time (departure and arrival), not just the time.
Photo & screenshot uploads are switched on — attach tickets and confirmations to any step or activity.
Added a sample packing list to the France demo trip so the Mine / Partner / Shared filters have something to show.

releases.title: Your trip, on a timeline
notes: A warm new look — light theme by default, a polished dark mode, and self-hosted typography.
Home lists your trips; open one to see it as a vertical timeline of travel legs and stays.
Each stay now shows its activities nested underneath, with 'book ahead' flags and map links.
Tap any activity to open its details and jot notes — a scratchpad per activity, with its own map link.
Tap a step's or activity's actual cost or booking status to edit it inline; costs show in the entry currency with a euro equivalent.
A Budget page totals everything in euros — estimated, actual, and projected vs your target — with a bar that turns red if you're heading over.
A Packing page: shared or personal items with a packed checkbox, quantities and categories, and Mine / Partner / Shared filters.
Attach photos and screenshots (tickets, confirmations) to any step or activity, with captions.
Deleted something by accident? Trash keeps removed steps, activities and packing items so you can restore them — or delete them for good.

releases.title: Infrastructure live
notes: Cloudflare Pages + D1 + Access are live; the site is gated by email one-time PIN.
GitHub CI is wired: PRs get a demo-mode preview, merges to main deploy production.
This note shipped through the PR pipeline itself — the parallel-session workflow works.

releases.title: Project skeleton
notes: Scaffolded the AI-first Cloudflare app: static SPA, /api Functions, shared domain core, D1 schema.
Included the remote MCP server (worker-mcp) so the app can be operated by talking to Claude.
Wired the GitHub parallel-session flow: branch -> PR -> gated demo preview -> deterministic merge.
